transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-07-01 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Rajiv Patel (Atlas BI - Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Atlas BI - Data Eng), Evan Cole (Atlas BI - Product)

Summary: Short sync to go over the latest quality eval run, surface regressions, and agree on tuning steps for prompt guardrails and a perf run on the quantized model variant. Some transcription noise and mis-heard product names.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we planned 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Rajiv: Hey, Rajiv here.
[00:08] Sofia: Sofia on from data eng.
[00:10] Evan: Evan, product.
[00:12] Jordan: And Maya is on the line, our SE, go ahead Maya.
[00:15] Maya: Morning all, hi.
[00:18] Jordan: Cool, agenda — quick results recap, highlight regressions, decide prompt edits and guardrail tuning, then perf next steps.

[00:30] Jordan: So we ran the main eval set last night, that spreadsheet I shared, top-level — overall pass rate for the core 2k prompts was 82%. That's automated metrics plus human spot-checks.
[00:45] Rajiv: 82, okay. What's our pass definition? Do we require exact match or acceptable completion?
[00:50] Jordan: Good question. It's a combined rubric: factual correctness for extraction prompts, then product-guideline match for tone / style. We mark as fail if hallucination or PII leakage.
[01:05] Sofia: Got it, any major clusters of failures?
[01:08] Maya: There are three clusters — one is PII exposures on long context prompts, two is hallucinated numerics in our finance queries, and three is formatting issues for table outputs.
[01:20] Evan: Formatting is high priority for our UI, that one hurts product acceptance.

[01:35] Jordan: I'll call out a few example fails from the sheet — prompt 482 where it included a SSN-like string in the reply, that was flagged by our heuristics and by human reviewer.
[01:50] Rajiv: Hmm, that suggests the redaction/guardrail didn't trigger. Are you running the guardrail step in the pipeline or post-hoc?
[01:58] Maya: Right now it's a post-processing rule plus a model filter. We saw a couple of cases where the filter missed because the entity was masked oddly in the context and the model paraphrased it.
[02:12] Sofia: We can probably normalize the input context on our side to help, strip non-standard separators.

[02:25] Jordan: Also saw a regression relative to last week's run on the 'sales-summary' prompt set — about a 6% drop. Could be noise but worth investigating.
[02:36] Rajiv: Any hypothesis? Model version change?
[02:39] Maya: We didn't change the model, same base variant, but we did flip a sampling temperature in the eval harness — that could account for some variance. Also context length distribution shifted; more long documents in this run.
[02:55] Evan: So is this because of cache/KV issues or purely sampling?
[02:58] Maya: Unclear; KV/cache should be stable for inference but longer context can increase hallucination surface.

[03:12] Jordan: On the perf side, Rajiv asked about quantized runs — Maya, you did an initial 8-bit run earlier this week?
[03:20] Maya: Yeah we did a smoke test. Latency went down ~22% p50 and cost per token dropped ~30% on our bench, but quality delta for a handful of prompts showed a small drop — mostly on numeric precision and some rare tokenization artifacts.
[03:36] Rajiv: 22% is promising for cost. But numeric precision hits our finance extraction. How bad was it?
[03:42] Maya: For extraction prompts, F1 dropped from 0.96 to 0.92 on average in the sample. It's not catastrophic but for edge SLAs that's material.
[03:52] Sofia: Could we run selective quantization — host non-sensitive flows on quantized and keep critical extraction on full-precision?
[03:58] Jordan: Yep that's a pattern we've seen — route by policy. Redwood can auto-route by prompt tag or latency budget.

[04:10] Rajiv: Regarding guardrails, what options do we have short term to prevent PII leakage?
[04:14] Maya: Short term: stricter regex-based post-processing, prefix-deny tokens, and model-safety prompts (few-shot safety examples). Mid-term: integrate KMS-backed redaction, pipeline-level normalization, and model-based PII detection.
[04:35] Evan: How fast can we iterate on guardrail tuning? We need to show product-safe behavior for demo next week.
[04:40] Jordan: We can do a targeted guardrail sweep in 3 business days if Atlas provides the red-team examples; that'll let us tune thresholds and update post-process rules.
[04:50] Rajiv: I'll ask my team to pull together 100 PII/high-risk examples and some negative cases. Expect by Monday.
[04:58] Sofia: On logs, we'll send a sanitized sample of our query corpus; there's a small work to normalize separators.
[05:05] Maya: For regressions, recommend we run ablations: rerun with prior sampling params, compare tokenization diffs, and look at context-length buckets. We'll share a small script to reproduce the eval harness.
[05:20] Jordan: Next steps recap: Jordan shares full sheet, Maya runs quantized perf + shares numbers, Rajiv sends PII examples, Sofia sends sanitized logs. Schedule security review if pilot goes green.
[05:35] Evan: Sounds good. Anything else?
[05:38] Jordan: Nope, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the doc and set up the security slot if needed.

End of transcript.
